All model architectures and fixed preprocessing were chosen using primary model cards, not optimized on these labels; nevertheless this is an exploratory search across multiple models on already-seen public development datasets.
Models learned from generic third-party pretraining, not consented app outcomes. Original training overlap with public documents is unknown.
Full-text neural and lexical retrieval similarity does not measure candidate consent, eligibility, essential qualifications, reciprocal interest, or hiring success.

TalentCLEF profiles are synthetic with expert relevance labels; all public English development judgments are positives; unlisted pairs remain unjudged. MAP is published-positive retrieval quality, not percent accuracy.
Crossencoder is reported only on the human benchmark, uses official pair input with longest-first512-token truncation, and may omit document tails.
BGE and E5 retain all document tokens with fixed448-token overlapping windows and equal mean aggregation; this can dilute specific facts and overweight overlap.
Fixed equal reciprocal-rank fusion uses k60 and midranks for ties; all explored variants are reported, not only the winner.
No neural method is promoted based on these public experiments; production learned promotion requires consented outcomes, held-out validation, versioning, and deterministic fallback.
